entry.title: Podcast: Rethinking Data: Moving From the Traditional Three-Tier Web Stack to Client-Side Event Sourcing (Source: feed.infoq.com)
entry.summary: Johannes Schickling explores how he moved beyond the traditional three-tier web stack to a local-first approach. He shares his experience transitioning from Prisma to developing Overtone-a music curation app leveraging client-side event sourcing and SQLite. The discussion highlights the trade-offs between event sourcing and CRDTs. By Johannes Schickling

entry.title: Airbus Makes Protection from Extraterritorial Law a Scored Criterion in its Cloud Tender (Source: feed.infoq.com)
entry.summary: Airbus selected Scaleway as its sovereign cloud provider after a tender that scored protection against non-European extraterritorial legislation alongside technical capability. Airbus frames it as complementing multi-cloud, not exiting AWS. Practitioners note the pattern is spreading past hyperscalers to small US SaaS vendors, and that sovereignty claims still require verifiable controls. By Steef-Jan Wiggers

entry.title: Presentation: Compiling Workflows into Databases: the Architecture That Shouldn't Work (But Does) (Source: feed.infoq.com)
entry.summary: Jeremy Edberg & Qian Li discuss why external orchestrators decrease reliability and how to use your existing database for durable execution. They share how DBOS Transact uses standard tables, SKIP LOCKED queues, and unique primary keys to manage complex, fault-tolerant AI workflows with minimal latency, all without the operational overhead of separate distributed systems. By Jeremy Edberg, Qian Li
